title: Tamsin and the Garden
premise: Tamsin Almeida, exiled for refusing to weaponize her storm-calling against civilians, survives as a smuggler in the Thornfell mountains until the night the border wards collapse and the stars vanish from the sky. Guiding a wounded stranger named Corin through the passes, she learns he carries proof that the usurper King Veylan's power—and the extinguished stars—stems from a stolen shard of the ancient Stormheart, an artifact whose loss once ignited the first war between humans and the sky-born. Hunted by Veylan's wardens and betrayed by the smuggler network that raised her, Tamsin must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the people who sheltered her. In the end, she shatters the Stormheart shard at the cost of her own storm-gift, restoring the stars but leaving herself ordinary—free at last to choose who she is.
about_author: Marguerite Hartwell is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy rooted in landscapes that feel like characters, drawing on folklore of borders, exile, and the price of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Smuggling moon-iron through Thornfell, she feels the border wards snap like cut harp strings as every star above the peaks goes dark. Her storm-sense screams warning while her caravan partner, old Bren, dismisses it as weather. The chapter ends with her finding a bloodied stranger collapsed on the high road—the first crack in her invisible life. Beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Broken Seal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She shelters the stranger, Corin, in a smuggler's cave and discovers a shattered seal branded into his palm bearing the sigil of the Stormheart—a symbol she knows only from exile-court legends. He begs passage to the free city of Vessa. Tamsin wants to refuse; helping him means becoming visible again. Beat: reluctant compassion overriding hard-won self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Warden Knows
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Pursued by warden-captain Ilse Varn, Corin reveals his mission: he was a royal archivist who stole proof that King Veylan's crown is powered by a stolen Stormheart shard, and that the extinguished stars are the sky-born dying. Tamsin realizes her exile was engineered by Veylan's court years ago. Beat: the vertigo of learning your whole life was someone else's chess move.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At a mountain tollhouse, Tamsin bargains with Maren, the smuggler queen who once mothered her, for safe passage down the Serpent Stair. Maren agrees—for a price: deliver Corin to her instead of Vessa. Tamsin lies and says yes, hiding the truth even from Bren. Beat: the first deliberate betrayal, committed to protect rather than harm.

chapters.title: Wardens on the Stair
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ilse Varn's wardens ambush them on the Serpent Stair. Cornered, Tamsin breaks her vow never to call storms again, summoning lightning that saves Corin but reveals her identity to every listening ear in the mountains. They escape into the deep caves, but Bren is captured covering their retreat. Beat: exhilaration curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Price of Old Loyalties
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Maren's riders find them; Tamsin must face the woman who raised her and confess her lie. Maren, revealed to be paid by Veylan's court, gives Tamsin a choice: hand over Corin or be cast out of the only family she has left. Tamsin chooses Corin. Beat: grief of severing the last tie to belonging.

chapters.title: Beneath the Sleeping Mountain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fleeing through the under-mountain roads, they reach the sealed vault where the Stormheart was first broken in the ancient war. Murals show the truth: the sky-born were not monsters but guardians, and Veylan's ancestors stole the shard to enslave the wards themselves. Tamsin's storm-gift resonates with the vault. Beat: awe and terrible understanding.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Road
chapters.summary: Corin's POV. Bren, broken by interrogation, has sold their route to Ilse Varn. The final chase begins through the Thornfell passes as Veylan's armies mass below for the assault on the free cities. Corin, feverish from his wound, confesses he may already be dying—and that only a storm-caller can carry the shard-proof into Vessa's heartstone. Beat: desperation fused with resolve.

chapters.title: Stormheart
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ilse corners them at the Vessa gates; Bren, having seen what Veylan's men truly are, turns his blade against the wardens and dies buying Tamsin minutes. Inside the heartstone chamber, Tamsin shatters the stolen shard with everything her gift can give, releasing the sky-born and reigniting the stars as her own storm-power burns away. Beat: sacrificial climax—victory purchased with identity itself.

chapters.title: An Ordinary Woman Under Open Stars
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later, Veylan's usurpation unravels as the restored sky-born testify before the free cities' council. Powerless now, Tamsin declines honors and a place in the new order, choosing instead to walk the mountain roads as a guide—no longer hiding, simply free. Corin, recovering, asks where she'll go. She smiles: everywhere. Beat: quiet, earned peace and self-possession.
